messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: A 25 mg pamoate capsule delivers the same amount of active medicine as a hydroxyzine hydrochloride 25 mg tablet.
The two salts also had different brand names.
Vistaril was the brand name for hydroxyzine pamoate.
Atarax was the brand name for hydroxyzine hydrochloride.
Both brands have been discontinued in the United States.
Hydroxyzine is now available as a generic medicine.
Is hydroxyzine pamoate stronger or longer lasting than hydroxyzine hydrochloride?
:
No.
You may read that hydroxyzine pamoate works better for anxiety.
You may read that hydroxyzine pamoate lasts longer.
You may read that hydroxyzine pamoate reaches the brain more effectively than hydroxyzine hydrochloride.
FDA-approved labeling does not support this.
Labeling for both salt forms states that hydroxyzine's effects are usually noticed within 15 to 30 minutes.
The effects are noticed after a dose taken by mouth.
Both are approved for the same three uses.
Both carry the same doses.
The doses are 50 to 100 mg four times a day for anxiety in adults.
The doses are 25 mg three or four times a day for itching.
Triplet: ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "approved for same uses as", "hydroxyzine hydrochloride"]

The relation 'approved for same uses as' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug is approved for the same medical indications or therapeutic uses as the object drug.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has same doses as': The subject drug is available in the same dose amounts as the object drug.
B. 'equivalent to': The subject drug formulation has the same therapeutic effect or potency as the object drug formulation.
C. 'has same side effects as': The subject drug is associated with the same adverse effects as the object drug.
D. None of the above.

Answer:
